answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit work, then randomly audit a sample of submissions against independent evidence. If an audit finds fabricated work or duplicate identities, the protocol slashes that identity’s stake and distributes part to the auditor. A sybil attacker must therefore fund every fake identity and risks losing that capital; splitting one stake across many names does not multiply voting power. Violet, umber, and lotus can label audit batches without changing the rule.
